clue.text: Released on bail in old England

indicators.note: letters released from their order are set free to form a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A suspect let out on bail somewhere in historic England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Released' looks like the start of a news report, but it tells you to rearrange ON and BAIL; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Albion is an ancient, poetic name for Britain, especially England.

indicators.note: most of the word, not all of it, is used, so its tail is cut off

parts.note: a la mode means in fashion

explanation.surface: A trendy Texan religious mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last two letters of ALAMODE. The Alamo is the San Antonio mission besieged in 1836.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was a Spanish Franciscan mission in San Antonio, famous for its 1836 siege.

clue.text: Bed and breakfast with neat compartment for small articles

parts.note: B and B is the usual short form for bed and breakfast
neat is an old word for cattle, so one beast is an ox

explanation.surface: A guesthouse offering a tidy cubbyhole for odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like 'tidy', but it is an old word for cattle, giving OX; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandbox is a light cardboard box for hats, collars and other small items.

clue.text: In respect of deliveries, there is strict OBE allocation

indicators.note: an allocation shares items out afresh, so these letters are dealt into a new order

parts.note: Officer of the Order of the British Empire, an honour, taken as written

explanation.surface: Honours are handed out under tight rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliveries' suggests post or honours handed over, but it means childbirth; 'allocation' rearranges STRICT and OBE, and 'there is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstetrics is the branch of medicine concerned with childbirth.

clue.text: A means of dating vehicle, fine in France

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle
bon is the French word for good or fine

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a car to take a date out, with a touch of French flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dating' suggests romance, but the definition refers to carbon dating, the method of ageing ancient material by radioactive decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiocarbon analysis lets scientists estimate the age of organic remains.

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river, praised as sweet in a song, an air

explanation.surface: A blossom whose scent hangs in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means something that flows, a river; Burns's song 'Flow gently, sweet Afton' calls this Scottish river sweet, and an 'air' is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: The Afton Water is a small Ayrshire river celebrated in a song by Robert Burns.

parts.note: capital investment is read as headgear put on, and the father is a priest

explanation.surface: A parent investing money in a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital investment' suggests finance, but it means something to cover the head (Latin 'caput'), and 'father' is a Roman Catholic priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy.

indicators.note: an installation puts things in place, so these letters are set up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: America keeps up its coastal military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Installation' looks like a base, but it rearranges US and INSHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed and sustain something is to keep it going.

clue.text: Leather straps attached to a jumper, for example

definitions.text: Leather straps attached to a jumper, for example

parts.words: Leather straps attached to a jumper, for example
parts.note: a jumper here is a horse that jumps fences, and the straps are the tack fitted to it

explanation.surface: Someone sewing leather strips onto a knitted sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a jumper is a sweater, which is the false picture; the clue means a show-jumping horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The set of straps by which a horse is fastened to a cart or controlled is its tack.

clue.text: People are up for this cup

definitions.text: People are up for this cup

parts.words: People are up for this cup
parts.note: riders who are 'up' in the saddle are handed a parting drink before setting off on a hunt

explanation.surface: Fans keen on a sports trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up for this cup' sounds like eagerness for a trophy; 'up' means mounted on horseback, and a stirrup cup is the drink served to riders before a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup cup is a farewell drink given to someone already mounted on horseback.

clue.text: At last, one is at work!

definitions.text: At last, one is at work!

parts.words: At last, one is at work!
parts.note: a last is the foot-shaped block a cobbler works on, so someone at it is busy making footwear

explanation.surface: Relief that someone has finally started working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At last' sounds like 'finally', but a last is the wooden foot-shaped form on which footwear is made.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler works with a last to make and mend footwear.

clue.text: Toast, in a way, is a feature of those who overeat

definitions.text: a feature of those who overeat

explanation.surface: A diner proposing a toast while getting fat from overeating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chin-chin' is a drinking toast, so a doubled 'chin' is that toast written one way; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The toast 'chin-chin' repeats one word twice, and a fold of fat under the jaw is common in heavy eaters.

explanation.surface: The dark outline cast by a railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' suggests a railway, but it means the trailing part of a gown; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone is to follow them secretly, and a gown's train is the long back part that trails behind.

explanation.surface: A soldier fighting against the government.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boxer Rebellion was an anti-foreign uprising in China around 1900; the question mark marks the second sense as a pugilist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese insurgents of 1900 were given this name, and a prizefighter in the ring has the same title.

explanation.surface: A helmet worn in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: Balaclava was an 1854 Crimean War battle, the one with the Charge of the Light Brigade; the knitted head covering is named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean War engagement of 1854 and the woollen head covering worn by soldiers there share the name.

indicators.note: served up like a dish, these letters are dished out in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these two words, with the S of the contraction, form the fodder

explanation.surface: Bundle yourself up warmly when afternoon tea is brought out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Served' suggests the tea being poured, but it tells you to rearrange WHEN TEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe or bind something in wrappings is to envelop it completely.

parts.note: arm-y signals are ones made with the arms, as with flags held out at angles

explanation.surface: The military's communications corps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' suggests soldiers, but read it as 'arm-y': signals made by holding the arms, with flags, in set positions.
explanation.definitionFit: This flag-signalling system spells out messages through arm positions.

parts.note: capital is read as belonging to the head, so the barren areas are bald patches of scalp

explanation.surface: Parts of a nation's capital city that are desolate wasteland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city, but it comes from Latin 'caput', head: the barren areas are patches of the scalp where hair has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical condition is hair loss, leaving bald patches on the scalp.

explanation.surface: A sluggish farmhand from a famous poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray's 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard' has the line 'The ploughman homeward plods his weary way'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogged, unhurried worker trudges on, as Gray's ploughman walks heavily home.

parts.note: the sovereign is a king of legend whose touch turned everything to gold

explanation.surface: A gold coin of the sovereign type.
explanation.walkthrough: A gold sovereign is an old British gold coin; here 'sovereign' means a monarch, the Phrygian king of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the king of Phrygia was granted a wish that everything he touched became gold.

parts.note: the Ribble is a river in Lancashire, northern England

explanation.surface: A dried-up river reduced to a feeble flow.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ribble is a river in north-west England; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny, thin flow of liquid is a slight seep.

explanation.surface: A radar return bouncing off a satellite in orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: Echo was the name of NASA's early balloon communications satellites of the 1960s; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflected radar pulse is a returned signal, and NASA named its first passive communications satellite this way.

clue.text: Cheese and crushed pear in fresh container

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, with the word for fresh as the container
names the word for fresh as the piece that holds the scrambled fruit letters

parts.note: fresh weather is cold, so chilly

indicators.note: crushed fruit is mashed out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Making a cheese course with mashed pear in a cool dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crushed' rearranges PEAR into AERP, and 'in' with 'container' puts that inside CHILLY, after its C. Caerphilly is a crumbly Welsh cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Caerphilly is a mild, crumbly white cheese from Wales.

indicators.note: a stormy sea is tossed about, so these letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that a small boat is unsuited to rough seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stormy' rearranges OCEAN; 'No' and 'for' are link words that make the surface true of the small boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light paddled boat, a small vessel.

indicators.note: a musical variation reworks a theme, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A broad, grand variation by the composer Elgar.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar wrote the 'Enigma Variations', so 'variation' fits the surface while telling you to rearrange ELGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and sweeping both describe something broad in extent or scope.

clue.text: Space at end of flight or passage

definitions.text: Space at end of flight or passage

parts.words: Space at end of flight or passage
parts.note: the flight is one of stairs, and the space is the level floor at the top; equally it is the arrival at the end of a voyage

explanation.surface: Room to stretch at the end of an air journey or sea crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests aircraft, but it is a flight of stairs, whose platform at the top fits the definition; it also names the arrival that ends a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: The level platform at the top of a staircase, or the act of coming ashore after a voyage, both bear this name.

clue.text: Oriole, a lower sort of flier

parts.note: something that lows, or moos, is a cow
a bird is a creature that flies

explanation.surface: An oriole described as a less elevated kind of bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' looks like 'more low', but it means one that lows, as cattle do. Cowbirds belong to the New World family that includes American orioles.
explanation.definitionFit: The New World cowbird belongs to the icterid family, which also includes the American orioles.

parts.note: greed is an excessive appetite

explanation.surface: An enormous appetite finally satisfied.
explanation.definitionFit: A settled matter has been decided by mutual consent.

explanation.surface: Honouring an American who rode by night.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Revere made a famous midnight ride in 1775 to warn of approaching British troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To venerate is to hold in deep respect, and Paul of that surname rode at midnight to alert the colonial militia.
